title: Paper Trading Has Blind Spots
topic: What paper-trading simulations omit and why a simulated fill is not a forecast of live execution

scenes.title: A PAPER FILL IS NOT A PROMISE
scenes.narration: A paper-trading fill can look convincing. But it is not proof that a live order would have filled the same way. The gap matters.

scenes.title: NO LIVE EXCHANGE ROUTING
scenes.narration: In Alpaca's paper environment, an order is not routed to a live exchange. The system simulates a fill using real-time quotes. That makes paper trading useful for testing code and workflow, but the result is still a simulation.

scenes.title: SOME COSTS ARE NOT MODELED
scenes.narration: The documentation lists important omissions: market impact, information leakage, price slippage caused by latency, queue position for non-marketable limit orders, price improvement, regulatory fees and dividends. Those effects can change a real outcome.

scenes.title: DISPLAYED LIQUIDITY MATTERS
scenes.overlay: A simulated fill can exceed shown size.
scenes.narration: There is another limitation. Order quantity is not checked against the displayed best bid and offer quantities, known as NBBO. A simulated order can receive a fill larger than the liquidity shown at that moment. Do not treat that as proof of real-world capacity.

scenes.title: SIMULATORS DIFFER
scenes.overlay: Fill, liquidity and data assumptions vary.
scenes.narration: Different simulators may also use different fill prices, liquidity assumptions, return calculations and market data sources. Results from one environment do not automatically transfer to another.

scenes.title: LOG THE LIMITATIONS
scenes.overlay: Paper results are not live results.
scenes.narration: Keep a paper-trading journal that names the simulator, data source and assumptions. Test conservative costs and partial execution scenarios where your tools allow it. Separate simulated outcomes from live-money performance. Paper-trading education only; not live-money performance; not investment advice; no guaranteed returns.

youtube_description:
A simulated fill is not a forecast of live execution. This short explains what Alpaca's published paper-trading documentation says the simulation does not model: market impact, information leakage, latency-related slippage, queue position for non-marketable limit orders, price improvement, regulatory fees and dividends. It also explains the displayed-liquidity limitation and why simulator assumptions differ.

claims.claim: Alpaca's paper environment does not route orders to a live exchange; it simulates fills using real-time quotes.

The published paper-versus-live limitations include market impact, information leakage, latency-related price slippage, queue position for non-marketable limit orders, price improvement, regulatory fees and dividends.
The paper environment does not check order quantity against NBBO quantities, so a simulated fill can exceed the displayed available liquidity.
Different paper-trading platforms may use different fill prices, fill assumptions, liquidity assumptions, return methodologies and market data sources.
